title: A frozen clip passes the loop-closure gate
body:
## Summary
A motionless clip measures 0 on all three seam axes and scores `pass`.

## Description
scripts/visual-gen/ardy/pof_loop_closure.py:61 and src/lib/motion-gate/loopClosure.ts:123 grade only the seam. A T-pose or frozen export has pose gap, worst joint and velocity jump of 0, so it reads as a perfect loop. The file's own honesty rule says an unmeasured verdict must never read as a pass. Fixed means the score refuses a clip with no motion, with a new per-clip motion amplitude.

## Flow
- Export a clip with identical frames
- scoreLoopClosure returns pass with reason 'Loops cleanly'
- Add a motion-range metric and return fail or n/a below a floor

## Expected impact
A frozen locomotion clip stops reaching the Blend Space as a clean loop. Could break: a legitimate idle with very low motion, so the floor needs calibrating.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the loop gate can tell a loop from no motion
Before: scoreLoopClosure({0,0,0}) = pass
After: not pass, once a motion floor exists
Method: simulation - walked the zero-metric case through the scorer; the fix sits in src/lib/motion-gate, outside this context's paths, and the floor needs real idle clips
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scoreLoopClosure over a synthetic frozen npz and real ARDY idle clips, both arms, to set the motion floor

title: Headless Blender renderers exit 0 when the script throws
body:
## Summary
The ARDY Blender scripts run without `--python-exit-code`, so a Python exception still exits 0.

## Description
scripts/visual-gen/ardy/pof_bvh_render.py:18 and pof_fbx_render.py:18 read `arm.animation_data.action` with no guard, and the documented invocations pass no `--python-exit-code` (zero hits in scripts/, src/, docs/animation-capture-pipeline.md). Blender's default exit is 0 after a script exception, so the only failure signal is a missing POF_RENDER_OK line. Fixed means a documented exit-code flag and an explicit no-animation error marker.

## Flow
- Run pof_fbx_render.py on an FBX with no action
- AttributeError prints, Blender exits 0
- Add the guard and pass --python-exit-code 1

## Expected impact
An operator or wrapper can trust the exit code. Could break nothing in-tree: no code spawns these scripts today.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed render is visible from the exit code
Before: exit 0 on exception (Blender default, not run here)
After: non-zero with a POF_RENDER_ERROR marker
Method: simulation - walked from source; a real Blender run was out of scope tonight
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Run each script headless in Blender 4.2 on an action-less file, both arms, and compare exit code and markers

title: POF_CRITIQUE and POF_LOOP markers are missing from the marker registry
body:
## Summary
script-markers.ts declares seven marker families, none of them this context's.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/script-markers.ts:48-102 is the 'one declaration' of marker keys for subprocesses PoF spawns, and critiqueMesh spawns pof_mesh_critique.py, yet POF_CRITIQUE_ is absent. Its keys live only in parseCritiqueMetrics. Fixed means the family is declared and a test asserts every key the Python emits is declared.

## Flow
- Add a key to pof_mesh_critique.py
- Nothing flags it as undeclared
- Register the family and derive a check from the script source

## Expected impact
Marker drift between script and parser becomes a test failure. Could break: the registry's own guard tests, which assume its current families.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one declared marker vocabulary
Before: 0 of 3 families (CRITIQUE, VLM, LOOP) declared
After: CRITIQUE at least declared and pinned
Method: probe - grep of prefix: lines in script-markers.ts; not built because the file sits outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: A test parsing emit() keys from the script against the registry, red before the family is added

title: npz concat truncates a fractional fps it timed sections with
body:
## Summary
Section starts use the float fps, but the merged archive stores int(fps).

## Description
scripts/visual-gen/ardy/pof_npz_concat.py:43 advances `t` by frames/fps with the float, and :46 writes `np.asarray(int(fps))`. At 29.97 the archive says 29, so the printed POF_SECTION_STARTS and the stored rate disagree by about 3 percent. ARDY exports are integer today, so this is latent. Fixed means storing the fps as read, once readers are checked.

## Flow
- Concatenate two 29.97 fps clips
- Archive fps = 29, starts computed at 29.97
- Store the float and confirm the npz readers accept it

## Expected impact
Montage sections line up for non-integer sources. Could break: a reader that assumes an integer fps member.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one frame rate per archive
Before: fps 29.97 stored as 29
After: stored as 29.97
Method: simulation - read from source; no fractional clip exists in the tree to probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Concat two synthetic 29.97 fps archives, both arms, and read fps back through src/lib/motion-gate/npz.ts

title: pof_fbx_render hardcodes 20 fps for every clip
body:
## Summary
The FBX reviewer forces 20 fps while both BVH paths take the rate from the file.

## Description
scripts/visual-gen/ardy/pof_fbx_render.py:20 sets `scene.render.fps = 20`, whereas pof_bvh_render.py:13 and pof_bvh_blender.py:14 import with update_scene_fps=True. A 30 fps UE export reviewed through this script plays at two thirds speed, so timing judged from the MP4 is wrong. Fixed means taking the rate from the imported action or a required argument.

## Flow
- Render a 30 fps UE FBX
- MP4 plays at 20 fps
- Pass the source rate through

## Expected impact
Reviewers judge retargeted timing at the real rate. Could break: existing MP4s compared against new ones.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - review playback matches the clip
Before: 20 fps regardless of source
After: source fps
Method: simulation - read from source; needs Blender and a UE export
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Render one 30 fps FBX in Blender 4.2 on both arms and compare MP4 duration to the clip

title: pof_bvh_blender overwrites one tile when the strip path is not .png
body:
## Summary
Tile names are derived with str.replace on '.png', so any other path collapses to a single file.

## Description
scripts/visual-gen/ardy/pof_bvh_blender.py:79 builds each tile with `strip_path.replace('.png', f'_{i}.png')`. For an uppercase .PNG or an extensionless path every iteration writes the same name, leaving one image while the final line reports `tiles: 6`. A path with .png earlier in a directory name is also rewritten. Fixed means os.path.splitext on the filename.

## Flow
- Pass strip.PNG
- All six renders overwrite strip.PNG
- tiles: 6 is still reported

## Expected impact
The scramble-check strip always has its six frames. Could break nothing: names are unchanged for ordinary .png paths.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the reported tile count matches the files
Before: 1 file for 6 tiles on a non-.png path
After: 6 files
Method: simulation - str.replace behaviour walked by hand; the module needs Blender fakes to probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Run the script under the BLENDER_FAKES harness with a .PNG path and count the render filepaths

title: The VLM reply protocol is parsed in four places
body:
## Summary
SCORE/DEFECTS/VERDICT parsing exists separately in two Python scripts and two TS gates.

## Description
scripts/visual-gen/pof_vlm_critique.py and pof_vlm_batch.py each carry parse_score, and src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts:51 and footage-gate.ts parse the same reply with their own rules. They have already diverged: before tonight only input-gate refused a score above 10. Fixed means one Python helper shared by the two scripts and a parity test against the TS parser. A shared import must still work under `python -I`, which drops the script directory from sys.path.

## Flow
- Add a reply format change
- Update four parsers by hand
- Extract the Python helper and pin TS parity with one fixture table

## Expected impact
A protocol change lands once. Could break: script invocation modes that rely on sys.path.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for one protocol
Before: 4 parsers
After: 2 parsers (1 Python, 1 TS) with a parity test
Method: probe - counted parser sites by grep; not built because it spans src/lib/visual-gen outside these paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: A shared fixture of replies run through every parser, with the disagreement count before and after
